title: Known bugs
objective: Fix the defects found while repairing zoom, the tools panel, contrast, the colour mixer and RAW editing, and while building the Performance section, on 2026-09-23.
context_summary: Each task is an independent defect with its measured symptom. None blocks the delivered behaviour; each is recorded so it is fixed deliberately rather than rediscovered.

tasks.description: Show no edited dot on a module band whose stored layer is neutral, such as Basic after its only changed field is reset to its default.
extra_context: The band's dot comes from `active` and `neutral` in the desktop's tools-panel state. `neutral` recognises the orientation identity, a whole-image crop and a RAW layer at As shot and 0 EV only.

A Basic layer left with every field at zero (for example after a double-click reset of Exposure) keeps the dot while its `recipe.describe` row reads Neutral. Presence, Colour mixer and Vignette layers left at neutral values are expected to behave the same way.

The dot reads the current entry's stored layers, not the displayed entry's rows, so it must not follow a historical preview. Prefer a neutrality answer owned by the core over more payload parsing in the desktop.

context_links.label: Tools-panel state
context_links.relevance: `active` and `neutral` decide the band's dot.

context_links.label: Develop workspace design
context_links.relevance: Defines the dot as a non-neutral layer in the current recipe.

acceptance_criteria: A stored Basic, Presence, Colour mixer or Vignette layer whose fields are all neutral shows no dot; any non-neutral field shows it.
Orientation, crop and RAW neutrality behave as today.
The rule that a payload is neutral is owned by the core, not re-derived in the desktop.

steps: Unit-test the dot for neutral and non-neutral layers of every module with a neutral form.
Extend a rendered scenario (`basic-panel` or `raw-panel`) to reset Basic's Exposure and assert the band has no dot.
expected_results: The dot follows whether the stored layer changes the picture, for every module.

tasks.description: Answer `render.sample` through a spatial layer off the catalog owner thread, so a pointer readout never delays another client's request.
extra_context: A point sample through a spatial layer now evaluates only the tile that contains its pixel on both paths, equal to the render by construction: about 20 ms with Clarity and 38 ms with Clarity and Dehaze on the Z6 and X100VI, 11 and 34 ms on a 24 MP JPEG. It still runs on the owner, so while another client samples in a loop every other owner call, the desktop's synchronous `draft.set` included, waits up to one sample: p50 19 to 20 ms against 0.3 ms idle, one to three frames at 120 Hz during a drag.

Proposed shape: the owner only plans the sample (state read, cached source verification, the draft's effective recipe when `draft_id` is named, an `O(layers)` compile, the prepared artifacts pinned), as `EditorService::sample_plan` already binds the current entry for capability tasks, and hands the plan with the call's own reply channel (`OwnerCall::response`) to a point worker that evaluates it and answers. The owner loop already answers the source-job methods outside the plain handler table; this would be the first method answered after the owner has moved on to other calls.

Clients see no change: the loopback transport serves each connection serially and every call carries its own reply channel. The answer keeps naming the entry and snapshot it was planned against, which the desktop already checks before showing a readout, and carries the event sequence the owner had when it planned the sample.

Bounds: one worker thread, blocked on its queue while idle (rule 8); a queue no longer than the live-client limit plus the desktop, since a connection has one call outstanding and the desktop keeps one sample in flight, with a full queue answering `resource-limit` (rule 6). A disconnect drops that client's queued sample. The readout is not on the gesture path, so the hop costs no frame under rule 12.
Keep the tile's input pull serial, or measure it again on the worker: pulled on the shared pool it waited behind a render holding the pool (p50 116 ms against 21 ms serially on the Z6).

Out of scope unless measured: the samplers a module's planning and queries use (`with_stage_context`) stay on the owner, because a commit is planned against them; in the canonical stage order their prefix holds no spatial layer.

Separately, the estimate store reduces the whole stage on a miss even when no unit asks for a global estimate (Clarity alone), which adds 23 to 113 ms to a stack's first sample on the owner; skipping that reduction is a small saving on both paths.

context_links.relevance: `OwnerCall` carries the reply channel; the loop's special-cased methods and its analysis worker are the pattern for a deferred answer and a bounded worker.

acceptance_criteria: `render.sample` through a spatial layer is evaluated off the owner on both paths, with the same request and response, and the sampled value still equals the full render's value at that pixel.

While another client samples in a loop over a real RAW with Presence, the desktop's `draft.set` and `asset.state` stay within a few milliseconds of their idle latency, measured on the Z6 and X100VI with load and sample counts recorded.
The worker sleeps when idle, its queue is bounded with a `resource-limit` answer when full, and a disconnect or a newer commit never shows a readout for the wrong entry.
The performance rules' known-costs row for the point-sample exception is updated to the owner-free cost.

steps: Core tests: a deferred sample answers the calling client in order, the queue bound refuses with `resource-limit`, a disconnect drops the queued sample, and the answer names the entry it was planned against across a concurrent commit.

Live-API measurement with two clients against a `develop --background` editor, one sampling in a loop and one timing `draft.set` and `asset.state`, before and after, back to back and reversed on the shared host.
A background evidence run with `hover` steps over a RAW with Presence.
expected_results: Hover readouts over a RAW with Presence stay exact and no other owner request waits behind them.

tasks.description: Stop a crop draft from hanging silently when its input-stage preview is superseded or cancelled.
extra_context: Opening a crop draft requests a truncated preview of the crop layer's input stage. If that job is superseded or cancelled before it answers, the pending draft is never opened and nothing tells the user; queued idle-section changes wait forever.
A render failure of the same job already ends the draft with a status; a cancellation does not.
A separate session is working on this.

context_links.label: Crop draft driver
context_links.relevance: Pending draft start, queued idle changes and draft end.

context_links.label: Single-image crop contract
context_links.relevance: Draft lifecycle and failure behaviour.

acceptance_criteria: A superseded or cancelled input-stage job either re-requests the stage or ends the pending draft with a visible reason.
Queued idle changes are replayed or dropped consistently with that outcome.
A scripted draft step settles instead of waiting for its deadline.

steps: App test that cancels the pending draft's preview job and asserts the outcome and status.
expected_results: No crop draft start can hang without a visible reason.

tasks.description: Make the `raw-panel` scenario pass on the DJI Air 2S, whose approximate white-balance drag frame misses the one-code average agreement check.
extra_context: `raw-panel` on the Air 2S fails the check that the released exact frame is within one code of the drafted approximate frame on average: 1.226 codes was measured.

The approximation's error is larger on the Air 2S than on the Z6 and X100VI: at 3200 K about 10% of display-proxy pixels differ by more than two codes (mean red error 1.23 codes), concentrated on glittering water and sand, where the demosaic's nonlinearity under a strong gain change dominates.
Decide between improving the approximation for such scenes and a per-source threshold justified by the measurements; the release always lands the exact frame.

acceptance_criteria: `raw-panel` passes on the Z6, X100VI and Air 2S.

expected_results: The scenario passes on every supplied RAW with an honest, documented tolerance.

tasks.description: Bound the display proxy of a tightly cropped RAW to the size the display needs.
extra_context: The proxy fits the crop's output to the display bounds, so a tight crop's proxy source approaches the source's own size: a 1801 × 1574 crop of the X100VI built a 7363 × 4909 proxy (414 MiB of float planes).
With a Presence layer on that crop each commit took about 8.7 s and the process peaked at 3.9 GiB RSS. The documents state this behaviour; nothing bounds it.
A candidate is to build the proxy over the crop's input region plus the resample margin, so the proxy is display-sized whatever the crop.

context_links.relevance: Proxy bounds and the proxy-equals-exact-downscale guarantee.

context_links.relevance: The recorded proxy memory figures.

acceptance_criteria: A cropped RAW's proxy source is bounded by the display bounds and a stated margin, independent of how tight the crop is.
Commit time and peak memory for the X100VI tight crop with Presence are measured before and after.
The proxy still equals the exact recipe rendered against the exact downscale.

steps: Core tests for the bounded proxy over a cropped linear source.
Measure the X100VI tight-crop journey with Presence before and after.
expected_results: Tight crops preview at display cost and memory.

tasks.description: Have the core report the crop layer's input stage instead of the desktop deriving it for the idle crop section.
extra_context: To show which ratio the committed crop reads as, the desktop folds the orientation layers over the photo's dimensions to size the crop's input stage, a copy of a geometry rule the core owns. It shows Free whenever any other geometry layer precedes the crop.
A clean fix is for `recipe.describe` (or an equivalent query) to report each layer's input stage, with UI/API parity.

The idle crop section shows the committed ratio for every stack the core can describe.

steps: Core test for the reported input stage through orientation and other geometry layers.
expected_results: One geometry rule, owned by the core.

tasks.description: Make Presence exact renders on large images use the cores they have.
extra_context: Measured by the performance smoke scenario and the Performance section on the owner's M4 Pro (14 cores) on 2026-09-23, at load 10 to 30: on the generated 60 MP JPEG an exact render with Clarity 100 took about 0.6 s, Texture and Clarity 7.2 s and all three Presence fields 17.8 s, while the process used only 135 to 190% of one core.

Suspects to measure first: tile batches held to one or two by the 256 MiB spatial target once each tile's working set carries every unit's halo, serial global estimates, or stages that run one after another with little parallel work in each. The spatial budget's peak is reported by `resources.read` under `budgets.spatial`.
A separate session is investigating this.

context_links.label: Spatial primitive
context_links.relevance: Tile batching under the spatial target, halos and global estimates.

context_links.label: Rendering and limits
context_links.relevance: The spatial stage boundary, 512 px tiles and the 256 MiB target that sets batch concurrency.

context_links.label: Rendering memory decision
context_links.relevance: Budgets are targets that keep memory low, not limits that refuse work.

acceptance_criteria: The cause is measured on 24 MP and 60 MP with each Presence combination: wall time, CPU use and the spatial budget's peak, with host load and sample counts.
A fix or a proposal with its memory and latency trade-off for the owner; exactness tests keep passing and output bytes do not change.

steps: Release measurements of Presence exact renders on the generated 24 MP and 60 MP JPEGs before and after, back to back and reversed on the shared host.
expected_results: Presence renders on large images use most of the machine's cores, or the owner has a measured proposal.

tasks.description: Make the desktop's capability journey test wait for the install to report progress instead of reading it at once.
extra_context: `the_whole_journey_goes_through_consent_jobs_and_apply_with_no_secret_anywhere` asserts that the resource install's row already carries a progress fraction immediately after the grant retries the install. On 2026-09-23 it failed once during a full `cargo xtask check` at a load near 20 (`installing.progress` was `None`) and passed on seven reruns, alone and with the whole desktop suite: the install job had not yet reported progress when the row was read.

context_links.label: Capability journey test
context_links.relevance: The progress assertion right after the grant and the install are sent.

acceptance_criteria: The test polls the tracked job until it reports progress, with a deadline, before asserting the fraction's range, and keeps asserting that the row reads Installing.

steps: Run the desktop suite repeatedly under load, for example beside `cargo xtask check` in another worktree.
expected_results: No failure across repeated loaded runs.
